scope: source-only; built under the owner's limited dependency exception against the reviewed COL-143 interface (hosted Storage proof open); hosted, device, staff and operating acceptance outside this review
method: Two independent read-only reviewers on the uncommitted tree of codex/hfo-col146-recovery. TypeScript: recovery library, client machine, hook, notice and five draft routes against the contract, with empirical runs of the machine (truncated and empty 2xx, HTML refusals, two-tab resume) and a real axe check; cross-checked against migration 345 once it existed. SQL: migration 345, its probe and race script against the contract and the 337–344 guarantees, with rolled-back experiments on the run-owned native cluster (other actor, other organisation, revoked and expired grants, signed-out session, new session, hash canonicalisation, key reuse on another occurrence). Both ran the gates; every finding was dispositioned and remediated; both reviewers re-verified.

typescript_review.verdict: changes requested (one blocker, four should-fix, notes) → re-verified PASS against the final 345

findings.claim: a 2xx whose body could not be read (connection cut mid-body, empty body) and a non-JSON 4xx were classified as usable refusals, so a committed save was shown 'Not saved' and its draft discarded
findings.disposition: Fixed: any unparseable body and any non-2xx JSON without a string error is a lost answer that reconciles; only a JSON refusal with a string error is the server's decision; tests drive a truncated 2xx through the machine to `saved` with no discard.

findings.claim: stricter than COL-145's correct route (required entry_reason on late/on-behalf corrections) and stored untrimmed values via passthrough, which could turn a resume replay into a different-content conflict
findings.disposition: Fixed: reason-carried semantics mirrored, strict object returning trimmed parsed output; rebase marker to import COL-145's schemas.

findings.claim: draft-level refusals mapped as record conflicts and retry() discarded without reconciling, so a second tab could show 'Not saved' for a saved record
findings.disposition: Fixed: draft refusals mapped first; retry reconciles before rejecting; two-tab scenario ends saved with no discard.

findings.claim: 345 initially returned the full row without kind, so the client could never reach saved from a real reconcile
findings.disposition: Fixed on both sides: 345 returns { kind, id, replayed } (probe-pinned); the client also derives kind from the draft command for a bare row.

findings.claim: a reached-but-unconfirmed server reply reused the 'could not be reached' wording

findings.where: hook, 401 handling, discard guard, unused select, list tests
findings.claim: listedFor not reset on cleanup; 401 gave the generic check-failed text; isDiscardOutcome ignored draft.state; DRAFT_SELECT unused; settled states untested

clean: list and read paths filter organisation, actor and current site grant; other actors get 404, never 403
nothing persisted in the browser; per-actor machine dropped on actor change or sign-out with in-flight answers ignored
resume sends no body; edited content is never re-sent
never saved without a record id; resumed replies mapped exactly as the original routes
strict zod bodies with per-command argument schemas and the 64 KiB cap
accessible notice with a real axe check; design tokens verified by hand
every 345 wording maps to a bounded class without echoing DETAIL
focused suite 45 files / 434 tests, typecheck, lint PASS

sql_review.verdict: approve with one should-fix and notes → re-verified PASS

findings.claim: reconcile matched the record by request key and actor only, so a key reused on another occurrence reconciled the draft as saved with the wrong receipt (verified rolled back)
findings.disposition: Fixed: task_instance_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM the draft's target for receipts and issues; probe case (key reused on another occurrence → unsaved, draft pending); re-verified.

findings.claim: resume cannot mark expiry on touch because it raises; only reconcile marks
created_at is trusted from the row under the token (the probe relies on it to age drafts); expires_at, hash, revision and state are still derived
findings.disposition: Recorded; only token holders insert and save never passes it.

findings.claim: another actor's existing draft id answers 42501 while an unknown id answers P0002; ids are random uuids and the routes map both to 404
no run artefact existed and waited_on was asserted by design
findings.disposition: concurrency.txt written with a dated header and the migration hash; waited_on now read from pg_locks and asserted in all three cases.
Hidden from authenticated readers by the restrictive policy, same posture as receipts.

clean: RLS uses actor, organisation and COL-133 current authority; other actor, other organisation, revoked grant, expired grant and signed-out session see nothing and are denied on every command; same person from a new session resumes
arguments never in a RAISE, returned only to the owner, omitted from the list
resume forwards target, key and arguments from the row only; signatures match 341/344; exceptions propagate with DETAIL intact; draft stays pending on refusal; FOR UPDATE serialises resumes
server-side hash over {actor, command, target, arguments}; reordered keys replay
guard: no DELETE, token required, derived columns overridden on insert, identity immutable, forward-only states, TRUNCATE guard
grants: authenticated SELECT only; service_role nothing; wrappers INVOKER to authenticated; helpers revoked
